name: Dead Souls II
english_description: The real, self-identified 'Dead Souls Mud Library II' (public domain, released November 2006 by Cratylus) -- a genuinely distinct middle generation of the Dead Souls lineage, sitting between the Nightmare-IV-era snapshot this collection already hosts as dsI (1996-98, 2 domains) and the later 3.8.6-era copies ds386/deadsouls_fluffos (8 domains, COMPAT_MODE/MSSP/LIB_DAEMON scaffolding). Confirmed distinct by a structural and byte-level diff: 4 domains (campus, default, town, Ylsrim), 1937 files, a 747-line master.lpc close in size/shape to dsI's 749-line file but with real content differences (added globals, different load_access() body) and none of the 3.8.6 copies' feature-flag machinery. Ships a genuine first-boot admin-installation wizard (name/password/gender/display-name/email/real-name/race-selection, matching dsI's flow), full ordinary-player registration, and preloads a real Intermud-3 client that makes an outbound network connection at boot. Porting it surfaced the same old-MudOS 'TYPE array NAME' declaration dialect as dsI (432 sites), the .c-to-.lpc rename's fixed-width filename-slice arithmetic (including the command-dispatch table itself), the 'ref' reserved-keyword collision, this driver's OLD_ED build vs. the archive's new-style ed_start()/ed_cmd() API, missing get_root_uid()/get_bb_uid()/creator_file() master applies, and one severe original-archive logic bug (lib/comp/seal.lpc's eventOpen() passed an object where eventPick()'s string lock-id argument was expected) that alone broke ~195 files -- the single highest-impact fix in this port. Also recovered two Latin-1-encoded source files the mechanical GB18030 conversion garbled (a multilingual curse-word table and a raw byte-to-string lookup table). 1401/1407 files pass a full compile sweep; the 6 that don't are all non-preloaded, pre-existing content gaps predating this port (a deliberately-removed stargate system, a missing lib/capture.lpc component, a foreign-codebase remote-admin daemon, wizard debug scratch files).
